title: Juniper and the Parish
premise: When Rafael Nakamura is called to probate a will signed by town founder Edmund Parish — dead and buried for thirty years — the document's authenticity forces an exhumation that reveals an empty coffin. Rafael, who has spent fifteen years as the keeper of Juniper's legal secrets, discovers the will names them executor of an estate built on a buried crime: Parish faked his own death to escape prosecution for a fire that killed three people, and someone in town has been paying to keep him hidden ever since. As Rafael traces the annuity payments through decades of ledgers, they realize the statute of limitations expires in eleven days, and whoever arranged the empty coffin wants the truth to die with it. In the end, Rafael must choose between filing the truth away like everything else or burning their own reputation to expose that Parish has been living in plain sight as the town's quiet groundskeeper — and that his granddaughter knew all along.
about_author: W. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade handling probate files in coastal New England. They write mysteries about paper trails, buried ledgers, and the people towns trust to keep their secrets.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Rafael Nakamura, POV. A courier delivers a will dated six days after Edmund Parish's burial, notarized by a stamp Rafael personally retired years ago. The emotional beat is professional unease curdling into dread as Rafael recognizes the handwriting on the witness line: their own mentor, long dead.

chapters.title: Exhumation Order
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. A judge grants the exhumation over the objections of the Parish family and half the town council. At the graveside, the coffin lid comes up empty except for a ledger bound in green leather. Rafael feels the town's eyes shift from grief to suspicion — and onto them.

chapters.title: Green Leather
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV, with interludes from the ledger itself. The book records thirty years of anonymous annuity payments routed through the church restoration fund. The beat is vertigo: Rafael realizes they processed some of these disbursements themselves without ever asking where they went.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Maren Okafor, a journalist and Rafael's estranged cousin. She profiles Elias Wrenn, the cemetery groundskeeper everyone adores, and notices his hands are too soft for the work. Her beat is the thrill of a story colliding with guilt over what exposing it will cost Rafael.

chapters.title: Alibis, Thirty Years Old
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. Reconstructing the night of the 1995 fire, Rafael interviews three aging witnesses whose statements were never filed — including one who swears she saw Parish alive at the ferry dock. The beat is the slow horror of realizing the town chose its lie deliberately.

chapters.title: What the Mentor Knew
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. Searching their late mentor's storage unit, Rafael finds correspondence proving the old lawyer helped fake the death — and a letter addressed to Rafael, unopened for fifteen years. The beat is betrayal braided with tenderness; the mentor trusted Rafael to find this eventually.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Someone ransacks Rafael's office and steals the ledger; Maren photographs her backup copy hours before her apartment is broken into. The beat is escalating menace — the hidden hand behind the exhumation is now cleaning up, and it knows where they both live.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. Confronting Camille Parish, the founder's heir who demanded the exhumation, Rafael learns she engineered it: she found the annuity trail and wanted her inheritance freed from its condition — silence. Her beat is cold clarity; she never expected the coffin to be empty because she assumed he was dead.

chapters.title: Cemetery at Dusk
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and Maren. Following the payment route to its final address, they find Elias Wrenn — Edmund Parish — tending graves, waiting for them. He confesses to the fire, the flight, the bargain. The beat is terrible calm: an old man relieved to finally be caught before the statute runs out on his own terms.

chapters.title: Filed Under P
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. With two days left, Rafael files the confession, voids the will, and watches the town reckon with its founder's name on every street sign. Maren publishes; Camille contests nothing. The final beat is bittersweet release — Rafael empties fifteen years of alphabetized secrets into the record and, for the first time, sleeps with the office unlocked.
